note: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA. Verdicts follow the rule pre-registered in README.md: per-round paired delta (arm minus p1, same run, same round, same mode, same CPU identity) over 6 reversal-balanced rounds; an effect only when all paired deltas share a sign and |median| exceeds p1's own per-round range (peak RSS: and 1% of p1). Operator rule 2026-10-22: anything that degrades any non-Lambda path is never a general default; summarize.py guard() refuses a general default unless every required cell is present with min_rounds balanced rounds and clean, finite, identical evidence.
reproduce: python3 general/summarize.py <arm64 run> <x86 run> --out <dir> --verdicts general/verdicts.json --commit <analysis sha> --run-id <id>

e8.hypothesis: Six-thread KleidiAI load-time repack (GGML_KLEIDIAI_REPACK_THREADS=6) removes the serial repack cost off Lambda too, with no warm/forward/memory or answer change, and is inert where KleidiAI is absent (x86_64).
e8.conclusion: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA. 0xd40 local-file: load 8.085 -> 2.432 s (-5.668 s, 6/6 rounds, p1 range 0.447); memfd -5.677 s (range 0.213). Warm, first inference, 4,096-token forward and peak RSS no change. Answers bit-identical to the same run's P1 and to P1's 0xd40 reference (60/60 requests, 12/12 forwards). x86_64: KleidiAI cannot be compiled, so the change is not in the binary path; every metric no change, answers identical to x86 P1 (30/30, 6/6). Dormant (patched libs, switch unset): load +0.062 s inside p1's 0.447 s range, answers identical. Verdict: general default, with threads = the engine's thread count (the shipped value 6 matched THREADS=6 here).

e9.hypothesis: A KleidiAI-prepacked GGUF with the E9 loader skips the runtime repack off Lambda too; it must refuse rather than misread on a path without KleidiAI.
e9.conclusion: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA. 0xd40 local-file: load 8.085 -> 3.317 s (-4.804 s, 6/6); memfd -4.838 s; warm/forward/RSS no change; answers bit-identical (60/60, 12/12). Same rounds, E9 loads 0.884 s slower than E8 (local, threshold 0.116) and 0.809 s slower (memfd, threshold 0.163), with no other difference: E8 is the better general mechanism. x86_64: the E9 GGUF is refused at load in 6/6 rounds, as designed; the E9 loader with a plain GGUF is inert (answers identical, timings no change). Hazard (October hazard/ files): an UNPATCHED P1 engine loads the E9 GGUF without error and returns NaN probabilities and wrong choices on arm64 and x86_64. A format that silently corrupts answers on any loader without the patch, and needs a KleidiAI build, cannot be a general default. Verdict: general opt-in (arm64 KleidiAI builds with the E9 loader only); prefer E8.

e7.hypothesis: Skipping the tied output head (LKAI_SKIP_TIED_OUTPUT=1) saves its repack time and memory on every decshim deployment.
e7.conclusion: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA. 0xd40 local-file: load -2.064 s (6/6), peak RSS -504 MB; memfd -2.041 s, -504 MB; warm/forward no change; answers bit-identical (60/60, 12/12). x86_64: peak RSS -576 MB (6/6, outside the 1% floor); timings no change inside the co-tenanted host's range; answers identical to x86 P1. Dormant: no change on both arches. No path degrades, but the switch aborts any request for logits, so it is only valid for engines that never ask for them (decshim). Verdict: general opt-in, default ON inside decshim-only deployments; not a llama.cpp-wide default.

e10.hypothesis: n_ctx 4096 (= the model's max_length) instead of 16384 cuts KV memory without changing answers or the 4,096-token forward.
e10.conclusion: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA. 0xd40: peak RSS -290 MB local and memfd (6/6); every timing no change (load -0.021 s local inside 0.447 s range; 4,096 forward -0.076 s inside 0.274 s); nothing worse. Answers bit-identical (60/60, 12/12 including the full 4,096-token forward). x86_64: peak RSS -281 MB, timings no change, answers identical. Verdict: general default, set from the head config's max_length rather than a literal 4096.

e5.hypothesis: Dropping the embedded tokenizer vocabulary (tokenizer.ggml.model=none) shortens GGUF load and memory for engines that tokenize outside llama.cpp.
e5.conclusion: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA. 0xd40: load -0.530 s local / -0.551 s memfd (6/6), peak RSS -83 MB; load+first request -0.536 / -0.385 s, inside p1's range (no change); warm/forward no change; answers bit-identical (60/60, 12/12). x86_64: peak RSS -54 MB, timings no change, answers identical. The file has no usable vocabulary, so any engine that tokenizes with llama.cpp (llama-cli, llama-server, generic GGUF consumers) cannot use it. Verdict: general opt-in for decider engines that tokenize in Python; publish beside, not instead of, the full GGUF.

e6.hypothesis: Shipping complete unchecked-hash bytecode cuts interpreter import time on every read-only deployment.
e6.conclusion: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA. 0xd40 (package mounted read-only): imports 0.484 -> 0.188 s (-0.296 s, 6/6, p1 range 0.059); load+first request -0.249 s inside range; load/warm/RSS no change; answers bit-identical (30/30, 6/6). x86_64 (same interleaved run, same compile rule via pyc_tree.py, 1035 compiled / 0 failed): imports +0.037 s median, no change: the co-tenanted host's p1 imports range is 1.409 s (loadavg 19-85), so x86 can only rule out a large regression, and none occurred; everything else no change, answers identical. It is a packaging step: on a writable filesystem CPython writes the same .pyc after the first start, so the gain there is the first start only. Verdict: general default for packaged builds (zip, container image, read-only mount), compiled with each target's own interpreter.

control_nan_fields_note: P1 itself returns these non-finite fields on x86_64 (libggml-cpu-sapphirerapids.so; README finding 2). Declared so the guard can require every OTHER answer to be finite and every arm to return exactly P1's set.
